answer: Each established agent is a lantern anchored to a cedar piling; to sponsor a newcomer it must lock a capital bond into a shared insurance reef. A random epoch audit that exposes one sybil claws the loss proportionally from every sponsor bond. So a fleet of masks needs real sponsors each risking real capital, and a single uncovered fake drains the whole reef, making attackers pay linearly in burned sponsor bonds rather than a one-time mint.
